update.title: [RISC-V][PR target/128139] Don't create pseudos when !can_create_pseudos_p on RISC-V
update.body:
Dumb mistake on my part.  When I added a new path to call synthesize_add I
didn't account for the possibility it could be called after the point where no
new pseudos are allowed.

The good news is that new path can handle synthesize_add returning false (no
synthesis available) so we just need to return false from synthesize_add if the
synthesis requires creating a new pseudo register (we could probably improve
that further by re-using the output if it doesn't overlap the register input,
but these paths should be very uncommon, so likely not worth the effort).

Regression tested on riscv32-elf and riscv64-elf.  K3, K1 and C920 are all
queued.  Pushing to the trunk.

	PR target/128139

	when !can_create_pseudos_p.

update.title: RISC-V: Disable RVV register overlap for vwabda[u].vv [PR target/128162]
update.body:
The widening absolute difference and accumulate insn vwabda[u].vv
reads the vd as the accumulator with EEW = 2 * SEW, while the vs1
and vs2 are read with EEW = SEW.  The section 5.2 of the vector spec
reserves any encoding in which one vector register supplies source
operands with two or more different EEWs.  Thus, the vs1 and vs2
must not overlap the vd register group, even in the highest-numbered
part.  But the Wvr constraint introduced by the commit 6df026ea07b
allows that, and we may have below asm dump.

  vwabda.vv v8,v9,v10   # LMUL = 1, SEW = 16

Disable the register overlap for vwabda[u].vv by the early clobber
vr, like the other widening multiply-add insns.

	PR target/128162

update.title: RISC-V: Add support for xxtvarith
update.body:
This patch adds intrinsic and auto vectorization (vec_perm) support for
xxtvarith, which is one of XuanTie's vendor vector extensions [1].  This
extension include xt.vile (vector interleave even) and xt.vilo (vector
interleave odd) instructions, that can be used for vector permutations
like [0, 8, 2, 10, 4, 12, 6, 14].  They can be useful for transpose
operations in workloads like x264.

Note that Zvzip also has similar instructions.  The same optimizations
can be applied when Zvzip becomes available.

Changes have been made based on suggestions by Robin since v1,
including VLA support and minor fixes.  Previous versions also contained
a coalesce optimization, which I decide to remove in this commit and
include in a follow-up.

Regtested on rv64gcv and rv32gcv, no regression.

[1] https://github.com/XUANTIE-RV/thead-extension-spec/blob/master/xxtvarith.adoc

update.title: RISC-V: add an "arch=" disassembler option
update.body:
The disassembler uses the ISA from the object's architecture attribute,
or rv64gc if there is none.  Some objects cannot carry the attribute.
A core file is one, and only the program that loads it knows the ISA.

Add an "arch=" option that overrides the ISA recorded in the object.
A "$xrv" mapping symbol still wins, since it names its own ISA.

The option sets the object's default ISA rather than being parsed once.
A bare "$x" mapping symbol returns to that default and would otherwise
drop the option.  An ISA string that does not parse is reported and
the previous ISA stays in effect.

Gas starts every code section with a "$xrv" symbol, so on an object
that still has its symbols the option has no effect.  The tests cover
both cases: on a stripped object "arch=" overrides the attribute, and
on the unstripped one the "$xrv" symbol wins until a bare "$x" returns
to the "arch=" ISA.

update.title: [PATCH] RISC-V: Keep whole-word tails in block-move group
update.body:
When a constant-size block copy has a size that is an exact multiple
of the word size and a copied word is immediately overwritten by a
later store, the pre-patch expansion defers the trailing whole word
to move_by_pieces, emitting its accesses after the group's stores.
RTL DSE then cannot prove that the trailing load does not read the
overwritten word, so it retains the dead copy pair, costing one dead
load and one dead store per overwritten word.

Keeping the trailing whole word in the group keeps all loads ahead of
all stores, which lets DSE remove the dead pair.  The new
cpymem-dse-1.c test (a copy whose Int_Comp word is immediately
overwritten; 48 bytes on rv32, 64 on rv64) flips from FAIL to PASS.

update.title: ivopts: Count register pressure in hard registers, not values
update.body:
ivopts_estimate_reg_pressure adds up the number of invariants, candidates
and other values live in the loop (regs_used) and compares that with
target_avail_regs.  target_avail_regs counts GENERAL_REGS hard registers,
and target_spill_cost is the cost of spilling one SImode register, so a
value that needs several registers is under-counted.  On GCN, where general
registers are 32-bit, every 64-bit pointer IV or invariant needs two SGPRs:
a loop with 50 such values needs 99 registers but was estimated at 50, and
the register-pressure cost stayed at 0 well past the real budget.

Keep a register total next to each value count.  Each candidate, invariant
variable and invariant expression gets a weight from
targetm.class_max_nregs (GENERAL_REGS, mode) for scalar integer modes (which
include pointers), and 1 otherwise.  Candidate weights are set in
determine_iv_cost; invariant weights are stored in two per-loop tables
indexed by invariant id and filled in determine_set_costs, after all
invariants are known and before the IV set search.  iv_ca keeps the register
totals in step with n_cands and n_invs at the four places that update them,
and only the register-pressure estimate switches to registers.  regs_used is
weighted the same way.

The other uses of the value counts are left alone: iv_ca_compare_deps still
compares numbers of invariants, and the pruning bound still counts IVs,
since they limit the search rather than estimate pressure.  Changing the
units of target_avail_regs in init_set_costs instead was rejected, because it
would also change what loop-invariant and predcom see.

On targets where pointers and word-sized integers fit in one general
register (x86_64, aarch64, rv64, ppc64), every weight is 1 and decisions
are unchanged.  32-bit targets with 64-bit IVs or invariants, such as
long long on i686, arm or rv32, now count them as two registers.

The ivopts details dump now shows registers and values in the regs_used
line and in a new "regs:" line for each IV set, and the "cost for size"
table is indexed by registers.

update.title: [RISC-V] Fix multiple small RISC-V bugs discovered during LLM review
update.body:
And yesterday's set of fixes inspired by LLM review of the RISC-V machine
description.

For ior/xor synthesis, two issues.  First we can trigger undefined behavior
with a shift by the size of the object.  It never results in incorrect code,
but it's best avoided.  Second, there's an off-by-1 error which caused us to
fail to synthesize the rotate variants in one class of cases.  The LLM
generated a test for the missed optimization.

For and synthesis, we could generate an unrecognizable insn if B is off, but
Zbkb was on.  It's an unlikely combination, but clearly wrong.  The LLM
generated a testcase for this problem too.

In the overflow expanders and divmod expanders, we can write the output before
the inputs are consumed.  This is actually safe in practice for these
expanders, but wrong from a design standpoint.  I don't have the md.texi or
rtl.texi passage handy, but the expanders are responsible for ensuring the
inputs are fully consumed before outputs are written.  make_safe_from handles
that nicely.  Given it's 100% latent, no testcase.

There's a unnamed define_insn_and_split that shifted 1, potentially by 32 or
more bits.  That's bad.  HOST_WIDE_INT_1U fixes that.  Didn't bother asking for
a testcase from the LLM

Regression tested on riscv32-elf and riscv64-elf.  Bootstrapped and regression
tested on the K3 and c920.  K1 is in flight.

	* config/riscv/riscv.cc (synthesize_xor): Avoid undefined shift when
	using rotate to get key bits into useful position.  Fix off-by-one
	error causing missed optimization in rotate case.
	(synthesize_and): Do not use zext.h if ZBB is not enabled.
	* config/riscv/riscv.md (addv<mode>4): Use make_safe_from to ensure inputs
	are not overwritten by early assignments to the output.
	(uaddv<mode>4, subv<mode>4, usubv<mode>4, <u>divmod<mode>4): Likewise.
	(addition with masked shift splitter): Use HOST_WIDE_INT_1U rather than 1.

update.title: [RISC-V] Fix miscellaneous bugs found by LLM review in RISC-V port
update.body:
Here's the next batch of things caught by LLM review of the RISC-V port.
Interestingly enough when I wiped memory and had it re-review bitmanip.md, it
did find one new thing, similarly for zicond.md.

So first, in the zero extension from HI expander.  If we're extending from a
promoted subreg, we can instead just generate a trivial move (which likely gets
optimized away).  That's fine and good.  But we failed to check that the inner
object's mode matches the destination mode for the extension.  It's easy enough
to check the modes.  While I've never seen this happen in practice, better to
be safe than trigger an obscure ICE one day.

In bitmanip.md we have a pattern which was not conditional on TARGET_64BIT, but
which extensively uses DI modes.  With only slight work we can make it
functional on rv32 as well (X mode and adjust hardcoded 63 to be BITS_PER_WORD
- 1.

In zicond.md there's an explicit subreg in the output pattern.  We just want
the lowpart, and if the operand was already a subreg, we'd end up with nested
subregs, which is verboten.  So we just construct a fresh operand with
gen_lowpart and use that instead.

riscv32-elf and riscv64-elf.

	subreg_lowpart rather than explicit subregs.

update.title: [RISC-V] Fix/simplify patterns for masked comparisons against zero
update.body:
Still digging through the various LLM spotted bugs.

In this episode we have 3 patterns which can simplify equality comparisons of a
masked register.  The precise form changes a bit, but the basic idea is to
right shift out as many bit positions as possible with the mask simplifying
down to a simm12 operand if at all possible. LLM review pointed out that the
split RTL in the second pattern would not generate valid RTL for any mode other
than word_mode.

The patterns were using ANYI iterators for the masking operation and its
operands, which in turn implies we're either doing a subreg or some kind of
extension in the split RTL.  While we can technically support ANYI here it adds
complexity for what appears to be no gain as I tried for a while (guiding the
LLM) to construct a suitable testcase.

Given the masking actually happens in word_mode, we might as well use X instead
of ANYI.  That also drops the subreg from the split-rtl.  If we do find a
testcase where matching ANYI would be helpful, we can always add it back and
we'll have a viable testcase.

Assisted-By: Claude for bug discovery and attempts to produce test

Tested on riscv32-elf and riscv64-elf.  Pushing to the trunk.
